title: Byblos
summary: Byblos is an ancient Mediterranean seaport on the coast of Lebanon, about 30 km north of Beirut, and one of the world's oldest continuously inhabited towns. Occupied since Neolithic times, it became a major trading centre exporting cedar to Egypt and is closely tied to the Phoenician alphabet. UNESCO listed it in 1984.
